reasoning: The failing assertion expects `.navbar-nav .nav-link` to have exactly 9 elements, but the app deterministically renders 10. Inspection of templates/base.html shows the menu contains 9 destination links (Home, Albums, Faces, People, Locations, Library, Sharing, Themes, Settings) plus one intentional assistant entry point: a `<button class="nav-link nav-assistant-toggle">` ("Ask Yaffo") rendered when `assistant_ready` is true. static/assistant/assistant.css confirms this item is deliberately shown in the collapsed Menu below 1200px and hidden on desktop in favor of a floating button. Additionally, the destination formerly labeled "Utilities" is now labeled "Library" (the utilities section was renamed app-wide). The spec goal — every primary destination stays reachable and all nine destinations are revealed — is still satisfied by the running application: all nine destination links are present and reachable, and the menu open/close behavior works (the test reached the count assertion after successfully opening the menu). The test is stale in two ways: its broad `.navbar-nav .nav-link` selector counts the assistant button as a 10th destination link, and its name list still expects the old "Utilities" label. The failure is deterministic (10 vs 9 on every retry), not a timeout or flake, and the app change is an intended feature rather than a regression.
affectedTests: Photo Gallery Feature - Responsive › gallery_menu_is_reachable_on_a_narrow_screen - every destination survives the collapse
suggestedAction: Update the test to match the current menu contract: assert the nine destination links via a link-specific selector (e.g. `page.locator('.navbar-nav a.nav-link')` toHaveCount(9)), change 'Utilities' to 'Library' in the destination name list, and optionally assert the 'Ask Yaffo' assistant button is also reachable in the open Menu.
